Championship|2006 San Antonio]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Kyle Colby Singler''' (born May 4, 1988){{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=1211259|title=Kyle Singler Bio|publisher=GoDuke.com|access-date=October 29, 2007|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924022902/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=1211259|url-status=dead}} is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Singler was a four-year starter for the [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke men's basketball team]] and was instrumental in their 2010 NCAA championship run, and was named the [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA Tournament's Most Outstanding Player]]. In the [[2011 NBA draft]], the [[Detroit Pistons]] selected Singler in the second round with the overall 33rd pick. His professional career spanned from 2011 to 2019. ==High school== Singler attended [[South Medford High School]] in [[Medford, Oregon]]. In high school, he averaged 29.3 points per game and 10.6 rebounds per game as a senior. In 2006, Singler played against [[Brandon Jennings]] in the championship game of [[The Les Schwab Invitational]]. Singler was also named to the 2006 U18 USA Junior National team, alongside fellow top prospects [[Michael Beasley]], [[Jerryd Bayless]], and 2006 star recruit [[Spencer Hawes]]. Singler is also one of eight players featured in [[Gunnin' for That No. 1 Spot|Gunnin' for That#1 Spot]], a 2008 documentary directed by [[Adam Yauch]] of the [[Beastie Boys]] which was filmed in 2006. In October 2006, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play college basketball at [[Duke Blue Devils basketball|Duke University]].{{cite news| last =Henry| first =Kris| title =Future looks bright for Singler, Blue Devils| work =Mail Tribune| date =October 28, 2006| url =http://www.mailtribune.com/archive/2006/1028/sport/stories/bk-nextkyle28.htm| archive-url =https://archive.today/20090221113256/http://www.mailtribune.com/archive/2006/1028/sport/stories/bk-nextkyle28.htm| url-status =dead| archive-date =February 21, 2009| access-date =February 21, 2007}} In 2007, Singler led South Medford to its first-ever state basketball championship, winning 58–54 over defending champion [[Lake Oswego High School|Lake Oswego]] and national standout [[Kevin Love (basketball)|Kevin Love]].{{cite news| last =Smith| first =Jeff| author2 =Freeman, Joe| title =It's Panthers' turn| work =The Oregonian| date =March 11, 2007| url =http://www.oregonlive.com/prepboysbasketball/oregonian/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fsports%2F1173599713127490.xml&coll=7| access-date =March 11, 2007| archive-date =March 15, 2009| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20090315034952/http://www.oregonlive.com/prepboysbasketball/oregonian/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fsports%2F1173599713127490.xml&coll=7| url-status =dead}} A year earlier, Love and Lake Oswego had defeated Singler and South Medford for the state championship. Singler was a member of the Legends [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, along with future [[UCLA]] player Kevin Love, and participated in many prestigious all-American camps, including the [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] All-American Camp (Indianapolis), the Nike Peach Jam ([[Augusta, Georgia|Augusta]]), and the Main Event ([[Las Vegas]]). ===Awards and honors=== * 2006 Elite 24 Hoops Classic * 2006 Second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] * 2007 Oregon Co-Player of the Year * 2007 First-team ''Parade'' All-American * 2007 McDonald's All American * 2007 Jordan Brand All-American * 2007 Oregon Southwest Conference Player of the Year * 2007 OSAA 6A All Tournament Team * 2007 OSAA 6A State Champion ==College career== === Freshman season (2007–2008) === [[File:Kyle Singler.jpg|200px|thumbnail|right|Singler during his tenure with Duke]] Singler started at [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] as a freshman and finished the 2007–08 season with averages of 13.3 points per game and 5.9 rebounds per game, helping lead Duke to a 28–6 record. Singler put to rest any speculation that he might enter the [[2008 NBA draft]], saying:
I didn't give the NBA any thought; I know I'm not ready. I need to mature both physically and mentally. I want to get stronger and quicker, and I want to work on learning how to play the game. I'm at a great place for that.{{cite news| last =Eggers| first =Kerry| title =Premature End Leaves Devil Blue| work =Portland Tribune| date =April 4, 2008| url =http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=120725473519946700| access-date =April 9, 2008| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20080411043630/http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=120725473519946700| archive-date =April 11, 2008| url-status =dead| df =mdy-all}}
=== Sophomore season (2008–2009) === In January 2009, he had a career-high 16 rebounds against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], a game in which Duke won 76–67. Singler ended the 2009 season as the top scorer for Duke.[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6469/kyle-singler ESPN – Kyle Singler Stats, News, Photos – Duke Blue Devils] At the end of the season, Singler was averaging a team-high 16.5 points per game in 37 games played.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kyle-singler-1.html|title=Kyle Singler|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|access-date=March 31, 2016}} === Junior season (2009–2010) === In February 2010, Singler scored a career-high 30 points against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], hitting a career-high 8 three-pointers in 10 attempts.{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/career-highs.php?playerid=2472 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |access-date=April 4, 2010}} In the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Tournament Final (playing Georgia Tech again), he hit a career-high 14 free throws. On March 28, 2010, in an [[Elite Eight]] NCAA game, as Duke beat [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and advanced to the [[Final Four]], Singler (667 points), [[Jon Scheyer]] (690 points), and [[Nolan Smith]] (628 points) became the second trio in the history of the school to score at least 600 points each in the same season. [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jason Williams]], [[Carlos Boozer]], and [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]] first accomplished that feat for Duke in 2001–02.{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040 |title=Notes: Duke 78, Baylor 71 – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |access-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-date=December 5, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205091943/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040 |url-status=dead }} Singler scored 19 points in the national championship game to reach 707 for the season, joining Scheyer (728) as the two became the second duo in Duke history to score over 700 points each in one season,{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204923002 |title=Notes: Duke 61, Butler 59 – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=December 5, 2009 |access-date=April 7, 2010}} following in the footsteps of [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jason Williams]] (841) and [[Shane Battier]] (778), who did so for Duke's 2001 national championship team. Through the 2009–10 season, Singler was also 6th on Duke's all-time list in offensive rebounds (272), and 7th in defensive rebounds (490).{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/misc.php?playerid=2472 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |date=May 4, 1988 |access-date=March 29, 2010}} For the season, he averaged 17.7 points and 7.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2010/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=5044890 |title=NCAA tournament: Duke Blue Devils' Lance Thomas and Kyle Singler pursue artistic side in the classroom – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 1, 2008 |access-date=April 1, 2010}} He was 3rd in the ACC in 3-point field goal percentage (.399), 4th in scoring, 3-point field goals made (2.1 per game; his 8 against Georgia Tech were the most in the ACC in a single game for the season), and minutes (35.9 per game), and 7th in free throw percentage (.798).{{cite web |url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2009-2010/confldrs.html#conf.wki |title=Atlantic Coast Conference Official Athletic Site – Men's Basketball |publisher=Theacc.com |access-date=April 3, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113130111/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2009-2010/confldrs.html#conf.wki |archive-date=January 13, 2010 }} Singler was instrumental in Duke winning its fourth national championship; he was named NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player after averaging 20.0 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game in wins over West Virginia and [[Butler University|Butler]]. Scheyer called him "the toughest player I've ever played with."{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/6713788/article-DuPree--Singler-earned-his-MVP?instance=most_popular |title=DuPree Singler earned his MVP |publisher=The Herald-Sun |access-date=April 2, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725215830/http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/6713788/article-DuPree--Singler-earned-his-MVP?instance=most_popular |archive-date=July 25, 2011 |url-status=dead }} === Senior season (2010–2011) === Following the national championship, Singler considered entering the [[2010 NBA draft]],{{cite web |last=Tysiacktysiac |first=Ken |url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2010/04/07/1361374/devils-should-have-talentto-make.html |title=Devils should have talentto make another NCAA run |publisher=CharlotteObserver.com |access-date=April 7, 2010 }} {{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} but ultimately decided to return for his senior season at Duke.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5115934|title=Singler to return to national champs|date=April 19, 2010|access-date=April 20, 2010|work=ESPN.com}} Singler was named the pre-season [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] player of the year, pre-season first team All-ACC, and was named a pre-season first team All-American. On November 27, 2010, Singler tied his career-high 30 points against his brother [[E. J. Singler]] and the [[Oregon Ducks]]. Singler was also voted to the Atlantic Coast Conference first team. For the 2010–2011 season, Singler averaged 16.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 1.6 assists in 34.8 minutes per game for the Blue Devils.[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kyle-singler-1.html Kyle Singler]. sports-reference.com The Blue Devils were eliminated in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet 16]] in the tournament against the [[Arizona Wildcats]] by the score of 93–77. Singler had 18 points in the defeat.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120714221004/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310830150|title=Derrick Williams, Arizona crush Duke's Tournament|Maui Invitational MVP]] (2008) == Professional career == ===Lucentum Alicante (2011)=== Singler was selected with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]].[http://www.detroitbadboys.com/2011/6/23/2240892/nba-draft-2011-detroit-pistons-draft-kyle-singler NBA Draft 2011: Detroit Pistons draft Kyle Singler] On August 23, 2011, he signed with [[CB Lucentum Alicante]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. The contract had an NBA out-clause for when the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]] ended.{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88188/lucentum-alicante-announces-rookie-kyle-singler.html |title=Lucentum Alicante announces rookie Kyle Singler |access-date=December 15, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215095423/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88188/lucentum-alicante-announces-rookie-kyle-singler.html |archive-date=December 15, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} In his Liga ACB debut, he won the MVP of the first match day with 23 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists. Following the conclusion of the lockout, Singler exercised his option to leave the club. In 10 appearances with Alicante, Singler helped them win 7 games while averaging 14.4 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals. === Real Madrid (2011–2012) === [[File:Kyle Singler Real Madrid (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Singler with Real Madrid in 2012]] Singler chose to join [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] on November 30, 2011, after the two clubs agreed on a transfer fee.[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=80685 Lucentum Alicante traspasa los derechos de Kyle Singler al Real Madrid] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215101017/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=80685 |date=December 15, 2014 }} {{in lang|es}} He went on to help Real Madrid defeat [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] to win the [[2012 Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|2012 Spanish King's Cup]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.dukechronicle.com/articles/2012/02/21/singler-and-pocius-help-real-madrid-copa-del-rey-title |title=Singler and Pocius help Real Madrid to Copa del Rey title |access-date=March 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140305155047/http://www.dukechronicle.com/articles/2012/02/21/singler-and-pocius-help-real-madrid-copa-del-rey-title |archive-date=March 5, 2014 |url-status=dead }} ===Detroit Pistons (2012–2015)=== [[File:Kyle singler pistons 2013 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Singler with the Detroit Pistons in 2013]] On July 11, 2012, Singler signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2012 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Forward Kyle Singler |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-forward-kyle-singler |access-date=2024-11-13 |website=nba.com |language=en}} He went on to earn All-Rookie second team honors in [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13]], averaging 8.8 points and 4.0 rebounds after playing in all 82 games.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2012-13 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2013|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On November 22, 2013, Singler scored a career-high 22 points in an 89–96 loss to the [[2013–14 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131122/ATLDET/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Hawks 96, Pistons 89 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 15, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630054858/http://www.nba.com/games/20131122/ATLDET/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 30, 2015 |url-status=dead }} Singler again played in all 82 games (including 36 starts) for Detroit during the[[2013–14 NBA season]], averaging 9.6 points and 3.7 rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2013-14 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2014|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Singler played in 58 games for the Pistons during the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]], recording averages of 7.1 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2014-15 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2015|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2015–2018)=== On February 19, 2015, Singler was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-team deal that also involved the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_150219|title=Thunder Acquires Kanter, Novak, Augustin, Singler and Draft Pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 20, 2015}} He made 26 appearances (18 starts) for Oklahoma City down the stretch, averaging 3.7 points and 2.1 rebounds. On July 9, 2015, Singler re-signed with the Thunder on a multi–year contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/singler_150709|title=Thunder Signs Singler to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}} For much of the first two months of the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]], he was a seldom-used, third-string forward off the bench. Between November 24 and New Year's Eve, Singler sat out eight games and twice played less than 60 seconds. Over the team's first 32 games of the season, Singler had made just six of his 31 three-point shots.{{cite web|last=Tramel|first=Berry|url=http://newsok.com/article/5473848|title=OKC Thunder: Kyle Singler returns from purgatory in win over Hornets|work=NewsOK.com|date=January 20, 2016|access-date=January 21, 2016}} He began to receive more game time in mid-January, and on January 20 against the [[2015–16 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]], Singler scored a season-high 11 points and hit 3–of–3 from three-point range.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160120/CHAOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Durant's 26 points lead Thunder past Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=January 20, 2016|access-date=January 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121050445/http://www.nba.com/games/20160120/CHAOKC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 21, 2016|url-status=dead}} In 68 appearances for the team, he posted averages of 3.4 points and 2.1 rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2015-16 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2016|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On April 9, 2017, Singler recorded eight points, four rebounds, three assists, and three steals during [[Russell Westbrook]]'s record-breaking 50-point [[triple-double]] game (Westbrook became the NBA's all-time leader in single season triple-doubles), a 106–105 win over the [[2016–17 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/400900576|title = Thunder vs. Nuggets - Box Score - April 9, 2017 - ESPN}} Singler made 32 appearances (including two starts) for Oklahoma City during the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]], averaging 2.8 points and 1.5 rebounds.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2016-17 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2017|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} In the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]], Singler made 12 appearances for the Thunder as a reserve, recording averages of 1.9 points, 0.8 rebounds, and 0.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Singler 2017-18 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/6469/type/nba/year/2018|access-date=August 26, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On August 30, 2018, Singler was waived by the Thunder using the stretch provision with two years remaining on his contract, meaning his salary stayed on the Thunder's payroll until 2022, long after his professional career ended in 2019.{{Cite web |date=2018-08-30 |title=Kyle Singler Reportedly Waived by Thunder Using Stretch Provision |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2793394-kyle-singler-reportedly-waived-by-thunder-using-stretch-provision
